result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A swaps every generic label and sample row for the gym's own words, turns the bottom form into real check-in, day-pass and shoe-rental tasks, and writes specific next-step messages. Its weak points are the prices it made up (flagged as placeholders but still shown on screen) and adding a whole script, which goes further than 'finish it'. B keeps the structure and invents nothing, but it leaves 'Total Users', 'John Doe', 'Item 1', 'Add New' and the Name/Value form as they were, so it misses the main request. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A keeps the page structure and invents nothing, but most of the generic content is still there: 'Total Users', 'Revenue', 'Active Items', John Doe, 'Item 1', 'Add New' and a Name/Value form. That leaves the screen looking as half done as before. B swaps in the gym's real tasks with clear forms (Check in, Sell Day Pass, Rent shoes). But it rebuilds much of the page, adds a localStorage app and puts made-up prices and pass types on screen, even though it flags the prices as placeholders. B comes out narrowly ahead because it fixes the main problem the user described.
